correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, an edge code with respect to selected landmarks is simply the selected-endpoint indicator vector: every nonendpoint landmark is distance one from the edge. Hence two omitted vertices in one part collide as vertices, and three omitted vertices always create two omitted-endpoint edges with identical all-one codes. With one omitted vertex, the only further obstruction is a selected vertex in a singleton other part colliding with its incident edge. With two omitted vertices, distinct parts and exactly two graph parts are necessary; each part must retain at least two selected vertices to separate endpoint incidents, which is equivalent to original part sizes at least three. These conditions are also sufficient by direct code comparison. A fresh direct computation gives \(\operatorname{mdim}(K_{3,3,5})=10\), and the frozen verifier exhausts all multipartite types through order ten.
correctness.risk: Finite exhaustive checks are corroborative; the all-partition theorem rests on the code classification.

final_claim: For every connected complete multipartite graph \(K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\), mixed resolving sets are exactly those whose complement is empty, or one vertex from a part while every other part is non-singleton, or two vertices from different parts in the complete-bipartite case with both parts of size at least three. Consequently the mixed-generator enumerator and corrected mixed metric dimension are exactly the stated \(N\), \(N-1\), and \(N-2\) cases, including \(\operatorname{mdim}(K_{3,3,5})=10\).
limitations: The complete-bipartite special-case dimension is prior coverage.
